# References with no document

**One thing puts a reference here: the archive could not get the document.**
Nothing under `md/` and `pdf/` carries this research, so there is something to
FETCH. Its two sibling reports are about references the archive DOES have:

| Report | The document | What is missing |
|---|---|---|
| document-gaps.md | not archived | the document itself |
| [review-gaps.md](review-gaps.md) | archived | a judgement that it came out right |
| [store-gaps.md](store-gaps.md) | archived | the source bytes it was made from |

Three shapes of the same problem, at different stages:

- **stub** - a file exists but carries a record rather than a document (its grade
  is `records`): a stub, a metadata-only page, a talk with no transcript.
- **unresolved** - no file at all, because conversion or the fetch failed.
- **broken capture** - a file was written from something that is not the
  document at all, so it was withdrawn.

A reference that HAS its archived Markdown and PDF is not listed here, even when
the content store no longer holds the bytes those files were made from. That is
a store-integrity fault, not an acquisition one: the document is archived and
published, and what is missing is the evidence behind it. Those are listed on
[store-gaps.md](store-gaps.md) so a reader of this file is never sent to fetch
something the archive already has.

A record that is a record BY NATURE - a CVE database row, a vendor advisory,
release notes, a package page - is not listed here either. Nothing is missing
from those; see [excluded.md](excluded.md) for the pages kept with no document.

Everything here is still CITED and still recorded in `manifest.json`.

Nothing here is lost work: the raw bytes of anything that was fetched are in the
content store, so a better converter or a different route is an offline re-run
(`refs.py acquire --force`), not a second crawl.

**This is the file to read if you want to fetch something a different way.**
Hand a file to the tool with `refs.py acquire --only <url>` after dropping it in,
or fix the route and re-run.
